title: Chipotle deploys 100 creators for latest ads spotlighting fresh food
tldr: Chipotle's first major push under CBO Fernando Machado lets 100 creators loose in its kitchens to spotlight fresh food, a concrete campaign breakdown of scaled creator-led content. Signals a shift from polished brand ads to distributed human creators.
why_fresh: scaled creator campaign as brand strategy shift
angle: What Chipotle's 100-creator model tells us about the death of the single hero ad and the rise of distributed human content.

title: Why Dr. Squatch is investing in experiences — not ads — with IShowSpeed
tldr: Unilever's Dr. Squatch is betting on co-creating content with Gen Z alongside top streamer IShowSpeed rather than running traditional ads. A case study in experience-led, audience-participation marketing.
angle: When brands stop making ads and start making moments: what Dr. Squatch's streamer bet means for content strategy.

title: AI is eating website traffic, websites are blocking AI – and reliable information is getting harder to find
tldr: The web's 30-year link-based social contract is collapsing as AI crawlers take content without referring traffic, prompting publishers to block them. Reliable information is getting harder to find as a result.
angle: The collapse of the link economy: how content strategists should rethink discoverability in an AI-answer world.

title: The Athletic teams up with sports creators to reach new (and younger) audiences
tldr: The Athletic is partnering with independent sports creators to reach younger audiences, a concrete example of legacy publishers borrowing creator distribution. Signals how media brands rethink reach through people, not just polish.
angle: Why publishers are outsourcing audience relationships to creators — and what they gain and lose.

title: How every major platform pays creators
tldr: A comprehensive breakdown of how each major platform monetizes creators, with varying thresholds and constant change. Useful reference for understanding creator-economy incentives.
why_fresh: useful roundup, not a new idea
angle: What platform payout structures reveal about where creators — and brand content — will migrate next.

title: The Best Brand Social Strategy Isn't Going Viral. It's Building Something People Miss
tldr: Argues the strongest brand social strategy isn't chasing virality but building consistent content audiences would actively miss if it stopped. A human-centered, retention-first take on social.
why_fresh: reframes success metric away from virality
angle: 'Content people would miss': a better north-star metric than reach or virality.

title: Mayor Mamdani's Friendly Influencers and the Funding of Public Messaging in New York City
tldr: CJR examines how NYC's new administration funds friendly influencers to spread public messaging, a look at the emerging paid-influencer civic-comms ecosystem. Raises governance and transparency questions.
angle: When institutions pay influencers to carry the message: the ethics of owned-influencer comms.

title: The New Burnout isn't about working too much. It's about working without meaning
tldr: A growing cohort of young workers reports burnout driven not by workload but by lack of meaning. Relevant for internal comms, employee engagement and change management.
angle: Meaning as an internal-comms mandate: how narrative combats the new burnout.

title: Did the rush of brands to Reddit kill the platform's ChatGPT citations?
tldr: As brands flood Reddit for AI-search visibility, the platform's authenticity — and its value as a ChatGPT citation source — may be eroding. A cautionary tale about brands overrunning organic communities.
why_fresh: brand influx vs AI-citation value tension
angle: How brand invasion destroys the authenticity that made a platform citable by AI.

title: California legislature passes a major local news funding bill
tldr: California passed AB 2222, creating refundable tax credits for newsrooms based on how many journalists they employ — potentially $40M/year. A novel headcount-linked funding model for local news.
angle: Paying for journalists, not clicks: what employment-linked funding means for media business models.

title: Are newspaper opinion sections embracing AI-written op-eds?
tldr: A WSJ op-ed by Stanley Druckenmiller sparked debate over AI-written opinion writing and where papers draw the line. Touches synthetic media, editorial governance and authenticity.
angle: When the byline is human but the words aren't: disclosure norms for AI-assisted thought leadership.

title: Lessons from a chief marketing officer turned content creator
tldr: A former CMO reflects on the shift to being a solo content creator, contrasting institutional and personal content-making. Useful perspective on executive positioning and personal brand.
angle: From brand voice to personal voice: what CMOs unlearn when they become creators.

title: How illustrator Azra Hirji turns the family table into an archive of food, migration and memory
tldr: An illustrator uses her Substack to preserve family recipes and migration stories through art, a striking example of intimate, human-centered narrative content. Story-scouting inspiration for personal archives as content.
angle: The archive as content format: turning personal memory into resonant visual storytelling.

title: Keeping cool when everything's on fire: Producer Marta Ravin's lessons
tldr: A veteran pop-culture TV producer shares lessons on staying composed under constant live pressure — transferable to crisis communications and issue management. People-over-panic craft wisdom.
angle: What live TV producers teach comms teams about grace under real-time pressure.
